title: HelperSSHToolSocketParams
description: Ask the far side for a TOOL SOCKET: a unix socket bound at a path the caller names, whose accepted connections this helper pipes into a socket on ITS OWN machine with the pane record written first (nocx-e2bws). It is its own op rather than a kind of `forward` because what arrives on it is not handed to the coordinator as a channel: the endpoint that admits an agent must be told WHICH PANE the connection belongs to before a byte of it is read, and only the party holding the listener can write that record.

destination.description: The connection the socket is requested on, and what to authenticate as: the same resolved triple `open` and `forward` take, resolved by the coordinator.

acceptOnTrust.description: The coordinator's answer to 'may a host key this host has never presented be recorded', carried for the same reason probe, open and forward carry it: this op may be the first contact with a host, and the helper may not decide that for itself.

hostKeyFingerprint.description: The key the caller expects for this destination, when it has one. Empty means it named none, which is the ordinary case for a direct connection and is refused for a linked credential by the coordinator before this request is ever built.

path.description: The socket path ON THE FAR HOST, as that host will see it. It must not exist when the request arrives — OpenSSH refuses to bind over an existing name rather than replacing it — and the directory holding it must already exist, because neither sshd nor this helper creates one: a helper that invented a path would be guessing about somebody else's filesystem.

target.description: The socket on THIS machine every accepted connection is piped into: the tool endpoint of the coordinator that asked for the pane, named by that coordinator per request rather than held by the daemon (one account's daemon serves several coordinators, D12).

session.description: The coordinator's session id for the pane these connections belong to. It is written before any far byte, and it is REQUIRED: a tool socket whose connections name no pane is a socket the coordinator can only refuse, so the request is refused by name before anything is dialed.
